title: Investigate missed calendar runs and overlap
goal: Prove one catch-up and active-service single-instance behavior.
challenge: Use the bounded worker to show missed-calendar catch-up once and no second active instance. No clock changes or universal cron serialization claim.

steps.command: ! getent passwd ll-s7 && ! getent group ll-s7 && test ! -e /home/ll-s7 && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash ll-s7 && test ! -e /etc/systemd/system/ll-s7.service && test ! -e /etc/systemd/system/ll-s7.timer && test "$(systemctl --no-pager show ll-s7.service -p LoadState --value)" = not-found && test "$(systemctl --no-pager show ll-s7.timer -p LoadState --value)" = not-found && test ! -e /etc/systemd/system/ll-s7-overlap.timer

printf '%s
' '#!/bin/bash' PATH=/usr/bin:/bin 'umask 077' '[ "$(id -un)" = ll-s7 ] || exit 2' 'cd /home/ll-s7 || exit 3' 'delay=$(cat delay); case "$delay" in 1|6) ;; *) exit 4 ;; esac' 'n=$(cat count 2>/dev/null || printf 0)' '[ "$n" -lt 4 ] || exit 0' 'n=$((n+1)); printf "%s
" "$n" > count' 'printf "BEGIN %s %s
" "$n" "$BASHPID" >> events' 'sleep "$delay"' 'printf "END %s
" "$n" >> events' | sudo tee /home/ll-s7/job.sh > /dev/null && sudo chown ll-s7:ll-s7 /home/ll-s7/job.sh && sudo chmod 0700 /home/ll-s7/job.sh; sudo runuser -u ll-s7 -- sh -c 'printf "1
" > /home/ll-s7/delay'
steps.explanation: Only1/6-second delay; four runs/eight short event lines maximum.

steps.command:
printf '%s
' '[Unit]' 'Description=Disposable scheduling practice' '[Service]' Type=exec User=ll-s7 Group=ll-s7 WorkingDirectory=/home/ll-s7 'ExecStart=/usr/bin/timeout -k 1s 10s /home/ll-s7/job.sh' UMask=0077 RuntimeMaxSec=8s MemoryMax=64M TasksMax=16 StandardOutput=null StandardError=journal | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/ll-s7.service > /dev/null; printf '%s
' '[Unit]' 'Description=Disposable calendar practice' '[Timer]' 'OnCalendar=*-*-* *:*:0/10' AccuracySec=1us Persistent=true Unit=ll-s7.service '[Install]' WantedBy=timers.target | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/ll-s7.timer > /dev/null; printf '%s
' '[Unit]' 'Description=Disposable calendar practice' '[Timer]' 'OnCalendar=*-*-* *:*:0/2' AccuracySec=1us Persistent=false Unit=ll-s7.service '[Install]' WantedBy=timers.target | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/ll-s7-overlap.timer > /dev/null
steps.explanation: Persistent10second and nonpersistent2second timers share one service.

steps.command: sudo systemctl --no-pager daemon-reload; sudo systemctl --no-pager start ll-s7.timer; end=$((SECONDS+15)); until sudo test -s /home/ll-s7/count; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 1; done; sudo systemctl --no-pager stop ll-s7.timer; end=$((SECONDS+10)); while systemctl --no-pager is-active --quiet ll-s7.service; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 1; done; before=$(sudo cat /home/ll-s7/count); sleep 25; sudo cat /home/ll-s7/count
steps.explanation: Stop after a prior run, wait25 real seconds over multiple missed slots.

steps.command: end=$((SECONDS+12)); until test "$(( $(date +%s) % 10 ))" -eq 2; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 0.1; done; sudo systemctl --no-pager start ll-s7.timer; end=$((SECONDS+3)); until test $(sudo cat /home/ll-s7/count) -gt "$before"; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 0.1; done; sudo systemctl --no-pager stop ll-s7.timer; printf "before=%s after=%s\n" "$before" "$(sudo cat /home/ll-s7/count)"; sudo cat /home/ll-s7/events
steps.explanation: Align away from next regular slot; reactivate briefly.
steps.expected: One catch-up increment, not each missed slot.

steps.command:
end=$((SECONDS+10)); while systemctl --no-pager is-active --quiet ll-s7.service; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 1; done; sudo runuser -u ll-s7 -- sh -c 'printf "0
" > /home/ll-s7/count; : > /home/ll-s7/events; printf "6
" > /home/ll-s7/delay'; sudo systemctl --no-pager start ll-s7-overlap.timer; end=$((SECONDS+10)); until test "$(systemctl --no-pager show ll-s7.service -p MainPID --value)" -gt 0; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 0.1; done; worker=$(systemctl --no-pager show ll-s7.service -p MainPID --value); sleep 3; current_worker=$(systemctl --no-pager show ll-s7.service -p MainPID --value); active_count=$(sudo cat /home/ll-s7/count); printf "worker=%s current=%s count=%s
" "$worker" "$(systemctl --no-pager show ll-s7.service -p MainPID --value)" "$(sudo cat /home/ll-s7/count)"; sudo systemctl --no-pager stop ll-s7-overlap.timer; end=$((SECONDS+10)); while systemctl --no-pager is-active --quiet ll-s7.service; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 1; done; sudo cat /home/ll-s7/events
steps.explanation: 6second worker spans2second slots; capture live PID/count after3seconds then stop further scheduling.
steps.expected: Same active PID/count1; BEGIN1 then END1, no second instance.

hints: Persistent applies to calendar timers only.
Use real elapsed intervals; do not move clocks.
An associated active service is left alone; independent services/cron are not universally serialized.
review: Stopped count and single catch-up before regular slot.
Live same PID/count and ordered BEGIN/END.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 107.2 partial cron/systemd timers; 105.2/108.2 reinforcement; self-reviewed, unscored. No at or full objective coverage.
